title: Derivative bound for a Gaussian indicator average
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\sin u\ne0$. For every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the derivative at $x$ of the Gaussian conditional indicator average with angle $u$ has norm at most
\[
n\left(1+\frac{1}{\sin^2 u}\right).
\]
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, then $\|D u_u(x)\|\le n(1+1/\sin^2u)$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, with operator norm for the maximum norm.
